pages.text: In the morning, Mom called Taro. He had to sweep the whole porch before going out. Taro picked up the broom.
"Go ahead! I'll be there soon!" he called out the window. He wanted to finish quickly and play with Mumu.
Mumu waited under the well tree. The broom's swishing came from Taro's porch. Waiting was boring.
Mumu stood up three stones and threw a ball of leaves. Tap! One stone fell.
Mumu made a rule: knock down all three, then hop on one foot. Mumu hopped along.
Taro arrived. Mumu was laughing and hopping alone. Taro stopped short.
"Looks like Mumu has fun without me." Taro stood behind the tree, staring at his toes.
While throwing leaves, Mumu saw him. "Why are you standing there? This is a game for two!" Mumu waved.
Mumu explained: three stones, five balls of leaves, and hopping on one foot. Taro hopped, too.
More and more rules appeared. "Now throw with your eyes closed!" Taro closed his eyes and threw. The leaves stuck right to Mumu's head.
